priceBasis: primePriceUsdPerSqm = prime residential USD/m2. Knight Frank Wealth Report 2026 (Q4 2025, US$1m-buys-X-m2) where covered; otherwise prime-district estimates cross-checked against Numbeo city-centre averages and local market reports.

cities.name: Lisbon
cities.description: Seven hills, yellow trams and river light. Old tiled buildings are being restored one at a time, and this is where most property fortunes begin.

cities.name: London
cities.description: A global capital of finance, Georgian squares and converted warehouses. Eye-wateringly expensive, yet it never really goes out of fashion.

cities.name: Miami
cities.description: Beaches, art deco and a skyline that keeps on climbing. Money pours in from across the Americas, and hurricane season makes insurance worth every cent.

cities.name: Mumbai
cities.description: India's restless commercial capital, where old mill land becomes glass towers and a sea-view flat costs more than most people can imagine.

cities.name: New York
cities.description: Brownstones, lofts and towers that scrape the clouds. Every square foot of Manhattan is fought over, and the deals here make careers.

cities.name: Dubai
cities.description: Man-made islands, record-breaking towers and marinas full of yachts. Prices swing hard here, but the rental yields are hard to resist.

cities.name: Riyadh
cities.description: A desert capital rebuilding itself at breakneck speed: new metro lines, mud-brick heritage restored, and villa land in the north changing hands fast.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.description: The world's largest city runs like clockwork. Neon towers, quiet backstreet homes and an earthquake code that shapes every building.

cities.name: Singapore
cities.description: A spotless island city-state of gardens, towers and very strict rules. Land is scarce, demand is global, and prices rarely look back.

cities.name: Hong Kong
cities.description: Skyscrapers packed between mountain and harbour, where a parking space can cost as much as a house elsewhere. Typhoons and politics keep it tense.

cities.name: Shanghai
cities.description: Colonial banks on the Bund stare across the river at a forest of towers. Huge, fast and tightly regulated, with rents that lag far behind prices.

cities.name: Paris
cities.description: Haussmann boulevards, zinc rooftops and cafés on every corner. Supply barely moves, so a flat with a balcony and a view is a prize.

cities.name: Sydney
cities.description: Harbour views, golden beaches and an obsession with property. Waterfront homes here are some of the most expensive in the southern hemisphere.

cities.name: Toronto
cities.description: Canada's biggest city: a lakeside skyline of condo towers, leafy old neighbourhoods and one of the world's most diverse populations.

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.description: Hillside mansions, beach bungalows and a sprawl of studios and freeways. Sunshine sells every home here, but faults and wildfires lurk.

cities.name: São Paulo
cities.description: South America's financial engine: an endless sea of towers, rooftop helipads and hidden gardens. The currency swings, but so do the bargains.

cities.name: Seoul
cities.description: Palaces, mountains and high-rise apartment estates on both banks of the Han River. South of the river, a flat can cost a small fortune.

cities.name: Zurich
cities.description: Private banks, a crystal-clear lake and the Alps on the horizon. Calm, safe and fabulously expensive, it barely notices a recession.

cities.name: Istanbul
cities.description: Minarets, ferries and waterfront mansions on the strait between two continents. Prices race inflation, and the ground itself is never fully still.

cities.name: Mexico City
cities.description: A high-altitude megacity of tree-lined boulevards, colonial plazas and buzzing cafés. Yields are generous, but it sits on an old lakebed in quake country.

cities.name: Cape Town
cities.description: Table Mountain looms over beaches, vineyards and clifftop villas. Some of the world's best views sell for a fraction of European prices.

cities.name: Monaco
cities.description: Two square kilometres of superyachts, casinos and tax-free fortunes on the Riviera. The most expensive address on Earth, and the final test.
